strongest_recommendations: Fix the false 'c2c list --json collapses Unknown→alive:false' claim and re-decide the read path. Source (ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:648-652) emits `alive: true|false|null` — the tristate IS preserved (`Unknown` → `null`). The design's §2.7 (01-session-message-browser-design.md:184-188) builds its entire 'prefer reading registry.json directly + reimplement /proc liveness in Python' rationale on a premise that is factually wrong. Since `c2c list --json` already preserves the tristate, the simplest MVP path (shell out to `c2c list --json`, map null→Unknown) is fully viable and the design should adopt it rather than reimplementing `/proc/<pid>/stat` field-22 start-time parsing in Python (a real footgun: clock-tick units, PID reuse, the pid_start_time match the broker does). This removes a whole MED-risk workstream.

Stop calling the room double-store dedup the 'verified, #1 correctness lynchpin' — it is UNVERIFIED against live data. The live broker (rooms/swarm-lounge/) has meta.json + an EMPTY members.json (`[]`) and NO history.jsonl at all, and a scan of every archive/*.jsonl found ZERO rows with a `#` in to_alias. The dedup predicate has a real source basis (c2c_broker.ml:3406 `tagged_to = m.rm_alias ^ "#" ^ room_id`), but the design's own claim that the broker's 'Confirmed contents' include `rooms/<id>/history.jsonl` (01:68, 02 README:76) is false for this host. The whole Rooms tab + dedup golden screen rests on data that does not exist locally yet — the design must build the test fixture from the source-code format, not claim live verification, and must handle the empty-room / no-history case as the COMMON path, not an edge case.

Add a hard dependency-bootstrap risk line: `textual` is NOT installed in the system python3 (verified: `import textual` → Impor­tError). The 'ships today, zero coupling' framing (00-README:121, 01:215) understates this — every operator and every CI/snapshot run needs a working `.venv` with Textual+Rich. The re-exec-into-venv pattern (workflow_tui_app.py:15) papers over first-run, but the snapshot test tier (the agent-readable feedback loop the whole proposal hinges on) cannot run until that venv exists. Make `just browser-venv` / venv bootstrap a Phase-1 task-zero, not a footnote risk.
factual_or_data_errors: FALSE PREMISE (HIGH): 01-session-message-browser-design.md:184-188 states 'c2c list --json collapses Unknown→alive:false today.' Verified against ocaml/cli/c2c.ml:648-652: Unknown maps to `alive: null` (JSON null), NOT false. The tristate is already preserved over the wire. The design's quoted-block rationale for reimplementing liveness in Python is therefore unfounded.

UNVERIFIED-CLAIMED-AS-VERIFIED (HIGH): 00-README.md:76 and 01:66-69 list `rooms/<id>/history.jsonl` under 'Confirmed contents' / 'Verified live on host xsm.' The live broker rooms/swarm-lounge/ contains ONLY meta.json + members.json + members.lock — there is NO history.jsonl. The canonical room timeline the Rooms tab reads has never been observed on this host.

FABRICATED MOCKUP DATA (MED): 01 §4.3 mockup shows '#swarm-lounge ... members: 6 (5●1○)' and a populated history.jsonl timeline. Live members.json is `[]` (empty array) and there is no history. The member-breakdown bullet (01:354 'from members.json joined to registry liveness') cannot produce '5●1○' from `[]`. The mockup presents data the live broker cannot supply.

DEDUP CLAIM PARTIAL: The `#<room_id>` to_alias dedup format is real in source (c2c_broker.ml:3406) but ZERO live archive rows exhibit it (scanned all archive/*.jsonl: distinct to_alias = ['bakeoff-glm51-peer','bakeoff-glm51b-target'], 0 with '#'). So the 'dedup-room-not-in-dm' golden screen (01:462) must be a hand-built fixture; it is not exercising observed reality.

REGISTRY FIELD OVERSTATEMENT (MED): The Peers mockup (01 §4.1) shows `role coordinator`, `dnd:off`, `compacting:0%`, `last activity: 8s ago` prominently. Live registry.json has NO record carrying `role`, `dnd`, `compacting`, or `last_activity_ts` — even the richest live records stop at pid/pid_start_time/registered_at/canonical_alias. The design notes records 'may be ABSENT' (01:83) but the mockups present these absent fields as the default rendered state, implying richer data than the broker currently writes.

SCOPE-OF-LIFT OVERSTATEMENT (LOW): 'lift the workflow-TUI architecture near-verbatim' (00:10, 01:24, 01:209). workflow_tui.py is 1949 lines with ~340 workflow-domain-noun hits; the pure-render FUNCTIONS are not liftable — only the 3-file skeleton + snapshot harness pattern + ~525-line app shell are. 'near-verbatim' overstates reuse of the render layer, which is a c2c-noun rewrite.
feasibility_risks: Liveness in Python is harder than the fallback implies: reimplementing `registration_liveness_state` means reading /proc/<pid>/stat field 22 (starttime in clock ticks), matching it against the stored pid_start_time, AND replicating the Docker `.leases/<sid>` mtime path (c2c_broker.ml:1407, ~Docker mode). Getting PID-reuse + start-time matching wrong silently mislabels dead agents as alive. Given the alive:null tristate is already in `c2c list --json`, shelling out is strictly safer; the design's preference for in-Python liveness is a self-inflicted risk.

0600/0700 permissions are real and pervasive: archive/ and keys/ are drwx------ (0700); broker.log, registry.json, archive/*.jsonl, individual inbox.json are 0600/0700 (verified ls -la). The browser runs as the same Unix user so reads are fine, but: (a) the snapshot test fixtures must NOT copy real archive content to a world-readable tmp (01:489 notes this but it is a real CI hazard); (b) a multi-broker picker (list_all_broker_roots) crossing into other users' or sandboxed roots will hit EACCES — needs graceful per-root error handling, not assumed.

DM-thread reconstruction cost is real and the MVP hand-waves it: to show A↔B (U2) the browser must scan archive/<A_sid>.jsonl AND archive/<B_sid>.jsonl AND map alias→session_id, but a single alias can have MULTIPLE session_ids over time (live registry shows bakeoff-glm51b-target and bakeoff-glm51b-dogfood sharing pid 2015845; aliases churn session_ids across restarts). 'map alias→session_id via registry' (01:94-98) assumes a 1:1 join that the data does not guarantee — an alias's full history may be sharded across several archive files whose session_ids are no longer in registry.json at all. The conversation abstraction (01 §4.2) is more expensive and lossy than stated.

broker.log rotation breaks a naive offset-tail: the design defers the events tab but if/when it lands, broker.log rotates (broker.log.1..N) at C2C_BROKER_LOG_MAX_BYTES (broker_log.ml:10,68) — a byte-offset tail (01:163 '(mtime, byte_offset)') silently loses events across a rotation. The same offset-tail strategy is proposed for archive/*.jsonl and history.jsonl; those are append-only and NOT rotated, so they're safe, but the design should explicitly note the events-log offset-tail needs rotation-aware logic.

Live-update via 1s full-restat does not actually scale to the merged views: 'set_interval(1.0), re-stat broker files' (01:140) is fine for registry + one room, but the Peers/DMs merged stream re-reads potentially every archive/*.jsonl on each peer selection; with many session_ids the per-refresh cost grows. The design says 'index once on load, incremental tail on mtime change' (01:488) but the mtime-gated incremental path is described, not designed — the interaction between 'select a different peer' (needs a full re-merge) and '1s poll' (incremental) is unspecified and is where real latency bugs live.

inotify upgrade path is fine here (inotifywait IS installed: /usr/bin/inotifywait verified) but is NOT recursive-safe on the broker at scale: `inotifywait -m -r` over the whole broker root watches archive/, keys/, .leases/, nudge/, rooms/ — including 0700 keys/ — and on some kernels hits the max_user_watches ceiling for large brokers; the design reuses the recipe verbatim (01:149) without scoping the watch to just the files the browser cares about.
scope_or_value_gaps: MVP value is thin against the empty live broker: with members.json=[] and no swarm-lounge history.jsonl on the actual host, the Rooms tab (a 'first-class, primary view' per 01:46) renders nothing today. The proposal's headline operator win (U3 'read the room') is the least demonstrable against real data. The design should re-rank: Peers + DMs are demonstrable now; Rooms is aspirational until rooms are actually populated — frame the MVP value honestly around what the live broker contains.

The proposal embeds a SECOND large workstream (the entire Part-B tmux-tool consolidation + Part-A role-wizard fixes in 02-existing-tui-polish.md) under the same campaign. Killing c2c-swarm.sh, porting restart/grep/follow, registry-first identity, the embedded-persona fallback — these are independently valuable but unrelated to the browser and inflate the apparent scope. They should be split into their own slice queue; bundling them risks the browser blocking on (or being blocked by) tmux-tool churn.

Read-only-with-no-send may under-deliver the actual operator need: the whole point of seeing 'A said X to B, B is stuck' is usually to intervene. Deferring send to Phase 3 (00 Decision 3) is defensible for speed but the design should pressure-test whether a pure read surface that still requires dropping to c2c_tmux.py to act is enough of a win to justify a new tool + runtime, vs. a smaller `c2c inbox/outbox/rooms` CLI (which the design itself floats at 01:507 as a 'stepping stone' and then under-weights).
open_questions: Does an alias reliably map to exactly one live session_id at browse time, and how should the browser present an alias whose historical archives belong to session_ids no longer in registry.json? (Live data shows aliases churning session_ids and sharing pids — the 1:1 alias→session_id join the DMs/Peers views assume is not guaranteed.)

Given c2c list --json ALREADY emits the tristate (alive: true/false/null), is there any remaining reason to reimplement /proc liveness in Python? If not, the §2.7 reimplementation paragraph should be deleted, not just softened.

Should the MVP ship the `c2c inbox/outbox/rooms` CLI stepping-stone FIRST (01:507-509) to validate the data model and dedup against real traffic before investing in the Textual layer + venv? The empty live rooms make this validation more valuable, not less.

Is the Textual/.venv runtime acceptable to Max at all, or does the absence of any Python TUI dep + the existence of inotifywait + the existing `c2c monitor`/`c2c list --json` plumbing tilt toward a smaller OCaml-CLI-plus-watch solution that needs no new runtime? The 'ships today' Python argument weakens once you count the venv bootstrap + the fact that the render layer is a rewrite anyway.

How does the browser behave under the documented RO-git-sandbox managed sessions? (Verified the broker root is under XDG_STATE_HOME, NOT .git/, so it escapes the sandbox — this is a POSITIVE the design should state explicitly as a feasibility win, since CLAUDE.md's whole broker-root redesign existed to dodge .git RO sandboxes.)

strongest_recommendations: KILLER FIRST VERSION = the Peers/roster pane + a live tail, NOT three tabs. Max's literal ask decomposes to two needs: (1) 'know who's alive' and (2) 'watch them talk without ssh-ing into panes.' The roster (Peers tab) with tristate liveness + role + idle-hint is the single highest-value artifact and it is ~80% already in `c2c list --json` + `registry.json`. Ship THAT first as the spine. The DMs-thread-reconstruction and the room-double-store-dedup are the most complex parts of the design and the LEAST exercised by real data (see factual errors). Recommend re-cutting the MVP to: Peers roster + a single unified live message feed (all DMs + room posts, newest-first, one scrolling pane) + 1s poll. Defer the per-peer thread view, the conversation-pair grouping, and the dedicated DMs tab to phase 2. This is a smaller, simpler v1 that delivers the actual deliverable sooner.

STRONGLY reconsider 'standalone Python tool, not a c2c subcommand.' Max's framing is 'without ssh-ing into tmux panes' — i.e. he wants ONE obvious thing to run. A standalone `scripts/browser/c2c_browser_app.py` with a `.venv` re-exec bootstrap is exactly the kind of discoverability friction the brief is complaining about. He will not remember `python3 scripts/browser/...` any more than he remembers `c2c agent refine`. Even if the implementation is Python, wrap it as `c2c watch` (or `c2c browser`) that shells out to the Python — a 5-line OCaml/justfile shim. The design treats 'standalone vs subcommand' as a deferred phase-3 decision; for a single-operator-tool UX it is a v1 decision. At minimum add a `just watch` recipe and a `c2c watch` passthrough so the entry point matches the muscle memory of every other c2c verb.

Validate the data model against REAL swarm traffic before building the snapshot-test edifice. The design specs ~8 golden screens including `dedup-room-not-in-dm`, but the live broker has ZERO room messages and ZERO `#room` archive rows — the dedup 'correctness lynchpin' is currently untestable against reality. Before committing to the full pure-render + golden-snapshot + tmux-QA harness (a real chunk of the build), stand up the `c2c_tmux inbox/outbox/rooms` CLI stepping-stone the design itself mentions (§9) and point it at a LIVE multi-agent session. That validates the dedup rule, the alias->session_id join, and the inbox+archive merge with one day of plumbing, and tells you whether the thread abstraction is even worth building, before any Textual code exists.

The role-wizard polish (doc 02 Part A) is worth doing but should be UNBUNDLED from the browser campaign and reframed as bug-fixes, not 'TUI polish.' A1 (embedded-persona fallback / dead-code) and A2 (refine hard-requires $TMUX, exits 1) are genuine correctness bugs that bite an operator today, independent of any browser — ship them as small standalone OCaml fixes. But the A3 'role-authoring form tab in the browser' is scope creep: it bolts a content-authoring surface onto a read-only message viewer, two unrelated concerns. Cut A3 from this campaign entirely. Verdict: do A1/A2/A4 as independent OCaml hygiene; drop A3.

Consolidate the tmux tooling (doc 02 Part B) is the right call and is arguably HIGHER immediate value than the browser for the actual phrase 'without ssh-ing into panes' — because `restart` (sends /exit, handles the 'Background work is running' dialog) only existing in the legacy bash script is a real operator footgun TODAY. Porting restart/grep/follow into `c2c_tmux.py` and deleting `c2c-swarm.sh` is a days-scale win with no new runtime. Recommend sequencing Part B's restart-port BEFORE the browser MVP, not as co-equal phase-0 work — it unblocks the operator faster and de-risks the 'two canonical tools' footgun the CLAUDE.md itself documents.
scope_or_value_gaps: OVER-ENGINEERED: the DM thread-reconstruction (§2.5, U2, the whole DMs tab) is the most complex subsystem in the design — per-session-id archive sharding, bidirectional merge across two archive files, frozenset conversation grouping, message_id dedup across an inbox/archive race — and it serves a use-case ('read a full A<->B thread') that is secondary to Max's primary ask ('watch them talk / who's alive'). The live broker has 3 conversation pairs total, all test traffic. This is building a threading engine before there is meaningful threaded conversation to read. Defer the entire conversation abstraction to phase 2 and ship a flat unified feed first.

MISSING what Max would actually reach for: a 'jump to this agent' affordance is correctly identified but deferred to phase 3 as a hard non-goal-adjacent feature. Yet 'watch them talk without ssh-ing into panes' implies that when something IS interesting, he wants to GO there. A read-only browser that can show him a juicy exchange but can't get him one keystroke closer to the pane is a frustrating dead-end. The 'o = open agent's tmux pane' binding (shell out to c2c_tmux.py enter) is cheap (the design already scoped it) and is the natural bridge — it should be in v1, not phase 3.

MISSING: no view of the agent's actual REASONING/work, only broker DMs. Max says 'watch my swarm of agents TALK to each other' — but the broker only captures explicit c2c sends, which are a thin slice of what an agent is doing. The pane scrollback (which the design correctly notes is lossy/ANSI-polluted) is ALSO the only place the agent's actual thinking/tool-calls are visible. The design frames pane-scraping as strictly-worse-and-to-be-subsumed, but for 'what is this agent DOING right now' the pane is the only source. The browser should acknowledge it shows the message layer, not the work layer, and keep the 'jump to pane' escape hatch first-class rather than positioning itself as a full replacement for looking at panes.

VALUE-vs-effort: the existing-TUI polish (doc 02) is worth doing but the docs over-weight it relative to the browser. The doc-02 'TUI polish' framing is partly a misnomer — there is no TUI to polish; it's CLI-formatter coloring (sessions/list liveness color) + tmux-tool consolidation + role-wizard bug-fixes. These are three unrelated workstreams stapled under one heading. The sessions/list liveness-coloring polish in particular is the lowest-value item (Max said he doesn't want to read CLI tables, he wants a live window) and should be the FIRST thing cut, not shipped in phase 0.
factual_or_data_errors: The 'room messages double-stored' dedup is presented as THE correctness lynchpin (HIGH severity risk, dedicated golden snapshot, 'the #1 thing to get right') but the LIVE broker on this host has ZERO room messages: `rooms/swarm-lounge/` contains only `meta.json` and `members.json` — `history.jsonl` does NOT exist — and `grep '#' in to_alias` across all archive/*.jsonl returns 0 rows. The dedup rule may well be correct per the OCaml source, but the design's confidence ('verified live on host xsm', mockups showing populated rooms) overstates what the live data demonstrates. The room-traffic path is effectively unverified against reality.

The ASCII mockups (00-README and 01 §4) depict a thriving 7-alive-agent swarm with active swarm-lounge chatter (coordinator1, lyra-quill, mm27-helio trading PASS/build messages, a live room watermark). The ACTUAL live broker: 7 registry records but 0 alive (all `alive:false`/`null`), 15 total archive rows ALL of which are bake-off test traffic (`bakeoff-glm51b-dogfood -> bakeoff-glm51b-target`, `nonexistent-sender-xyz`, etc.), 3 conversation pairs, no rooms populated. The mockups are aspirational fiction, not a render of real state — reasonable for a design doc, but a reviewer should know the populated-swarm scenario has never been observed in this broker.

01 §2.7 and 00 both lean on `c2c list --json` for the roster but the design's own caveat is understated: `c2c list --json` does NOT emit `role`, `last_activity_ts`, `dnd`, or `compacting` — verified output has only `{session_id, alias, pid?, alive, registered_at}`, and `alive` is a tristate-collapsed `true|false|null` (null = the Unknown case). So the Peers-tab mockup columns (role 'coord'/'agent', idle '120s', dnd, compacting%) CANNOT come from `c2c list --json`; they require reading `registry.json` directly AND those fields are frequently ABSENT (4 of 7 live records have only `alias/canonical_alias/registered_at/session_id` — no pid, no role, no last_activity_ts). The roster mockup shows data the substrate often does not contain; the design should show graceful-degradation states (role unknown, idle unknown) as the COMMON case, not the exception.

Minor: 00-README §3a/§3b and the doc map reference files `01-browser-tui-design.md` and `02-data-model-and-surfaces.md`, but the actual files on disk are `01-session-message-browser-design.md` (under `.collab/design/`, a DIFFERENT directory) and `02-existing-tui-polish.md`. The README's internal cross-references and document map do not match the real filenames/locations — a reviewer or implementer following the links will 404. The campaign's own file organization is inconsistent (design doc split across `.collab/research/` and `.collab/design/`).
feasibility_risks: The `.venv` + `maybe_reexec_textual_venv` bootstrap is itself a discoverability/reliability tax that cuts against the 'simple to run' goal. The workflow-TUI pattern works in a skill context where the venv is managed; bolting it into a c2c-repo operator tool means the first-run experience is 'pip install textual into a venv that may or may not exist,' which is exactly the friction Max is trying to escape. If Python/Textual is chosen, the venv bootstrap must be bulletproof and wrapped behind a single `c2c watch` / `just watch` entry, or the tool will rot unused like the role wizard it's meant to replace.

Snapshot-test determinism for a LIVE-data tool is harder than the design implies. The workflow-TUI golden-snapshot approach assumes fixture-driven render; but the browser's value IS live broker data. The design correctly calls for a fixture broker dir + pinned clock, but maintaining ~8 golden screens against an evolving registry/archive JSON schema (which the design itself notes has legacy/minimal-record variance) is ongoing maintenance the swarm must sustain. Given the schema already has 4-key-minimal records in the wild, the fixtures must cover the degraded cases or the snapshots will pass while the live tool shows blanks/crashes.

Live-tail correctness under the broker's atomic-rename writes: the design's 1s-poll + mtime/byte-offset tail of *.jsonl assumes append-only files that only grow. registry.json and *.inbox.json are REPLACED (temp+rename), not appended — fine for full-reread — but if any archive/history file is ever rotated/rewritten (the design notes broker.log IS rotated at 10MiB), the byte-offset tail will silently desync or replay. The design hand-waves this ('in-memory (mtime, offset) is sufficient'); needs an explicit 'if file shrank, reset offset and full-reread' guard or it will corrupt the live feed on the first rotation.
open_questions: Has the populated-swarm scenario in the mockups EVER been observed on this broker? If the swarm is rarely running 7 live agents trading room chatter, the browser's headline value (watch a busy live room) may be exercised only during surges. Worth confirming with Max what his actual day-to-day swarm size is — it changes whether the roster-only v1 or the full three-tab design matches reality.

Is 'watch them talk' satisfied by the BROKER message layer at all, or does Max actually mean 'watch what the agents are doing' (reasoning/tool-calls), which only lives in pane scrollback? These are different products. The design assumes the former; the brief's phrasing is ambiguous. This single question determines whether the browser is the right artifact or whether a better pane-aggregator (the read-half of c2c_tmux.py, made less lossy) is what he'd actually reach for.

Should role-wizard work (doc 02 Part A) be in this campaign at all? It is a separate concern (role authoring) bundled under a 'TUI review' heading mostly because the operator misremembered it as a TUI. Confirm with Max whether fixing the role wizard is in-scope for 'I want to watch my swarm' or a separate ask that got swept in.

Stepping-stone decision (design's own open Q3): ship `c2c_tmux inbox/outbox/rooms` as plain CLI BEFORE the Textual browser to validate the data model? Strongly recommend yes given the data-coverage gaps found here — but it needs an explicit go/no-go from the orchestrator because it front-loads a throwaway-ish surface.
